note: Additive merge of 5.1 polygons (136 incl. Frogmen, Hookfleet, Tiguantin, Andaru) + settlements upgraded with town, inhabited ruin, and fort pin stages.

polygons.name: Lake of Shim
polygons.notes: The lake Shim stands on (its eastern shore at px 382,788): the Shim river widened, about 32 by 12 km, the river entering from the south and leaving north. To carve like the Bay of Voth (tools/scale-model/features.py, the bay pass, at the land's level here). settlements/shim/PLAN.md; the owner, 2026-10-18.

polygons.name: rift rim N
polygons.notes: The N rim, the glass rim (biomes/riftrim/PLAN.md section 3). Split from 'rift rim' 2026-10-23; its west end follows the w rift highland's border.

polygons.name: rift rim S
polygons.notes: The S rim, the black rim (biomes/riftrim/PLAN.md section 3). Split from 'rift rim' 2026-10-23, with the west bend south of the w rift highland.

polygons.name: High Rift
polygons.notes: Propagating eastern tip of the Great Rift between Oidong Valley and Siphon Pits: Opaline Sinter Staircase, North Mirror Graben (Lake Verdigris & Lake Cinnabar), Dorsal Wedge median horst, South Fire-and-Ice Coulee, and The Singing Gjar.

polygons.name: Stalker Gate
polygons.notes: Multi-branch meandering mountain and highland pass network connecting the Yuni Emirate, Stalker Range (Hub 01), Loom-Chasms, Mid Basin, and Siphon Pits around Lake Vapora.

polygons.name: Mid Basin
polygons.notes: Volcano-tectonic transitional hinge zone between Siphon Pits and Loom-Chasms: Western Loess Corridor, faulted basalt relay benches, breached horseshoe maar-diatreme amphitheaters, and subterranean Ostrukh spring resurgences.

polygons.name: neo-ozarks
polygons.notes: Neo-Ozarks Dissected Carbonate & Porphyry Plateau (56,684 km²): an ancient epeirogenic tableland of flat-lying cherty dolomite and limestone (+1,260 to +1,680 m) deeply dissected by spring-fed hollows and first-magnitude karst caverns. Famous for its 5 strike-aligned exposed veins and knobs of purple-red rhyolite porphyry (+180 to +320 m ridges) where rivers carve boulder-choked canyon shut-ins.

polygons.name: sasquatch tribes
polygons.notes: Sasquatch Tribes High Periglacial Valleys (132,232 km²): a rugged northern rim territory east of the NW Outer Wall, cleaved by 4 steep-walled glaciated and periglacial U-troughs (Frost-Jaw Vale, Bone-Larch Hollow, Hoar-Wind Glen, and Scree-Tooth Basin at +5,850 to +6,240 m, 0.71–0.76 atm, ET/Dsc) smaller and harsher than the Yeti Kingdom's Cold Lake valley.

polygons.name: spider lake
polygons.notes: Spider Lake Highland Silk-Forest Basin (72,928 km²): centered on the +1,460.0 m hydrothermal highland lake (1.20 atm, 0.26 atm O₂, Cfa/Cfb). Sublacustrine warm seeps fuel year-round "lake-smoke" midge clouds that sustain permanent 200,000-strong colonies of eusocial spiders (Arachneapolita sericifera) and live rotational silk-weir arachniculture (see biomes/spiderlake/PLAN.md).

polygons.name: Silent Vales
polygons.notes: The Silent Vales (40,444 km²): an interconnected network of sheltered, fog-draped cool-temperate montane valleys (+1,135 to +1,890 m floors, Cfb/Csb) and two quiet ribbon lakes nestled behind the western coastal hogback ridge, draining west via a mossy water-gap gorge into the Crook River.

polygons.name: tsunami coast
polygons.notes: The Tsunami Coast (483,208 km²): northwestern mainland littoral zone repeatedly battered by tsunami trains generated by the explosive Steaming Seamounts. Features a wave-planed bedrock scour apron (+6 to +65 m in the SW funnel sector, +4 to +24 m in the NE Arch-shielded shadow), NW-to-SE V-shaped megatsunami boulder chevrons, backwash canyons, and perched saline plunge-pool lagoons.

polygons.name: ria valley
polygons.notes: The Great Ria River Valley: broad fertile alluvial and terraced valley sloping continuously from the Eastern Highland Lake (+1,460 m) and Tharn foothills westward to the Ring/NW Ocean. Once settled by the Ancients; hosts a rich hybrid ecology of Earthlike gallery forests, terraced orchards, and alien symbiotic flora.

polygons.name: double delta
polygons.notes: The Great Double Delta: a massive twin-lobed marshy tide-and-wave delta at 0.0 m basin/sea level receiving both the main Ria River from the east and the second Arch & Northern Massif river system from the northwest and north. Features colonial terrestrial sponges and calcified sea-pen fields.

polygons.name: arachnoid canyons
polygons.notes: Venusian Volcano-Tectonic Arachnoid Network & The Web-Cleaver Gorge: concentric ring-dike cauldrons and radial extensional fracture canyons straddling northern, eastern, and SW Korona and the southern Ria Valley rim. Cleaved by a dramatic 1,200–1,850 m-deep sinuous canyon carrying the Highland Lake river through northern Korona down into the Ria River.

polygons.name: the arch
polygons.notes: The Arch: an exposed undersea mid-ocean spreading ridge over the Steaming Sea (inspired by Capsica's Arch), featuring a double line of parallel rift-shoulder horst ridges (+750 to +2,150 m) with a lowered axial rift valley and drowned median sound in between, linking the northern Ria coast to the Crook.

polygons.name: steaming seamounts
polygons.notes: Steaming Sea Explosive Seamount Chain: a cluster of shoaling submarine volcanic calderas and Surtseyan/Krakatoan tuff cones centered in the western Arch. Periodic phreatomagmatic eruptions and flank collapses generate megatsunamis across the northwest ocean, making ports rare.

polygons.name: the crook
polygons.notes: The Crook: a deep tectonic trough squeezed between the western crater wall and the towering Western Boundary Cordillera. Opens at its northern neck into the Arch via a sea-level tidal fjord (0.0 m) and slopes continuously upward toward the south into a fumarolic and malachite-stained montane ecosystem.

polygons.name: copper glacier
polygons.notes: Copper Glacier & Crook–Rift Glacial Pass: a high-altitude alpine cryosphere in the southern Crook where glaciers grind through copper-porphyry, malachite, and azurite veins, tinting the banded ice verdigris-emerald and feeding the turquoise Copper Tarn (+2,380 m). A glaciated alpine pass extends east-southeast across the western rim to connect The Crook directly with the northwestern head of The Rift.

polygons.name: tharn uplands
polygons.notes: NE Tharn Uplands & Outer Rim: high, cold-dry windswept alpine and hypobaric outer-rim plateau (+5,800 to +9,800 m) inspired by Chris Wayan's Tharn, where high-elevation freeze-thaw aridity meets the airless outer crater rim.

polygons.name: outland gate
polygons.notes: Outland Gate (NE Trans-Boundary Water-Gap Pass): a dramatic highland valley and water-gap corridor (+1,460 to +1,734 m floor framed by +4,400..+7,600 m snow peaks) breaching the northeastern rim to carry the Outland Gate River from the northern Outland lake directly into Spider Lake (see biomes/outlandgate/PLAN.md).

polygons.name: ne outer wall
polygons.notes: NE Outer Wall — The Glass-Skarn Bastion (101,372 km²): a structurally unique impact-crater rim bastion wedged between the Northern Korona volcano-tectonic dome, the Arachnoid radial dike swarm, Spider Lake, and the Outland Gate fault. Features 3 geothermally heated Boxwork Dike-Cauldrons (+2,670 to +2,950 m warm hydrothermal tarns), pistachio-green epidote and wine-red grossular garnet contact-metamorphic skarn badlands, and black pseudotachylite fault mirrors.

polygons.name: godshearth
polygons.notes: A caldera cut into the Godthrone's south flank: floor 3.6-3.75 km, walls 3-4 km high, the hot lake (3,642 m) and the spillway south. Climate (the owner, 2026-11-09): cools with height, 6 C per km from a floor of +7 C (warm month 15 C, days 24 / nights +6; cold month -2 C, days +7 / nights -10, to -18 C in the cold-air pools on clear nights): Cwb on the floor, Dwb on the benches, Dwc and ET on the rim. Rain 750-925 mm, about 70% of it in the warm half as afternoon storms, so the nights and the winters are clear (the model holds annual rain only). biomes/godshearth/PLAN.md.

polygons.name: Greenstep
polygons.notes: Greenstep (renamed from Green Valley): the windward, rain-drenched counterpart of Godstep Valley, descending NNW across five ponded flood-basalt lava terraces (+3,180 m to +960 m) incised by two collapsed lava-tube rilles. Captures ~1,050–1,760 mm/yr of rain (Cfa/Cfb) from prevailing NW winds and serves as the greatest refuge of the Free Giants (the Vrivolci) and escaped slaves of every people fleeing the Vothic Kingdom and the Realm of Dalab, home to their cyclopean fortress of Tallwalls (Talodunon / Da-Talwal) at px 650, 1268 (biomes/greenstep/PLAN.md).

polygons.name: Labyrinth
polygons.notes: The Labyrinth (250,872 km²): a Martian Noctis Labyrinthus & E/NE Chaos Terrain inversion canyon complex carved into the 4.8–6.3 km SW Glaciated Dome. Progresses from beaded pit-crater catenae in the west/south through a 3-trend intersecting polyhedral fault-graben network in the center into a collapsed Martian Chaos Terrain of isolated flat-topped horst mesas and knobby pyramids in the east/northeast opening toward The Rift and Copper Glacier.

polygons.name: Stalker Peaks
polygons.notes: East of the Catch: the ranges from its eastern wall (7-11 km) to Hub 01's high valley (~4.4-6 km; Hub 01, the ruined arcology run by a mad AI, at 1344,1409) and the 12-15 km peaks round it (1287,1293; 1321,1481; 1397,1505; 1411,1409). The Stalkers' country; no caravan takes its passes. biomes/catch/PLAN.md section 6c; scale model 5.1 edit 3 (2026-11-11).

polygons.name: Andaru
polygons.notes: Throne vent-shoulder & ash-nomad kin of Zeijani (Ṣunu-Ašru & Šadū-Qarnu); raid colonizers, export fungal goods & Ranj.

new_user_settlements.name: Arfwai
new_user_settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: halfway (to Stair). Izani Afguai, Dasrī al-Ḥafwē, Xanadui Hāphwe; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1074 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 3 (2026-11-11).

new_user_settlements.name: Bitta
new_user_settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: bitter water: brackish, drinkable by beasts, not by people unless boiled with ash. Izani Bit'ar, Dasrī al-Bitar, Xanadui Biṭṭar; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1576 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 3 (2026-11-11).

new_user_settlements.name: Kolli
new_user_settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: the cold one: the first water down from the notch, snowmelt seeping at the north fan's toe. Izani Kold'a, Dasrī al-Kōl, Xanadui Kholṭu; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1446 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 3 (2026-11-11).

new_user_settlements.name: Lasso
new_user_settlements.notes: An oasis of the Catch's crossing: the last water before the southern passes, toward Strongbow. Izani Last'a Guat'ar, Dasrī al-Lāst, Xanadui Lāsṭu; caravaneers say whichever their master's tongue is. A spring and seep at a fan's toe: a pool, a reed bed, poplar and tamarisk, a well (1509 m). biomes/catch/PLAN.md sections 4 and 8; placed by scale model 5.1 edit 3 (2026-11-11).
